sentences.text: Atrociraptor marshalli was a small dromaeosaurid dinosaur estimated to be 1.8 to 2 meters long and weighing 15 kilograms.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, consists of four skull bones and several teeth, including the premaxillae, maxilla, and dentaries.
This animal possessed large arms, a long tail with rod-like extensions on the vertebrae, and a short, high skull that was unusual among its relatives.
While ten tooth sockets were found on the right side of the lower jaw and six on the left, researchers estimate the complete number was likely twelve or thirteen.
Wayne Marshall discovered a partial dromaeosaurid skull in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation near Drumheller, Alberta, in 1995.
Philip J. Currie and David Varricchio formally described the genus and species in 2004.
Studies suggest dromaeosaurids used their sickle-claws to grasp and restrain prey while dismembering them with their mouths, similar to modern birds of prey.
Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2016 that Atrociraptor could attack and wound relatively large prey more effectively than its relatives due to its strong head and teeth.

Powers and colleagues noted in 2022 that dromaeosaurids with deep maxillae, like Atrociraptor, were predators characterized by large size, serrated teeth, recurved claws, and a developed sense of smell.
Atrociraptor is classified as a member of the subfamily Eudromaeosauria within the family Dromaeosauridae, though it was initially placed in Velociraptorinae.
A 2009 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and Currie reclassified Atrociraptor into the subfamily Saurornitholestinae alongside Saurornitholestes.
Atrociraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age, approximately 68 million years ago.
The holotype comes from the Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, dating to 72.2–71.5 million years ago.
Scientists debate the dispersal pattern of Eudromaeosauria, with uncertainty regarding whether the group originated in North America or immigrated from Asia.
By 2012, there was no scientific consensus on the affinity of Atrociraptor to other dromaeosaurids due to conflicting phylogenetic analyses.
It is debated whether Atrociraptor moved elsewhere due to climate change or went extinct, as no remains have been found from the youngest sediments.
Isolated teeth previously referred to Saurornitholestes found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation may be assignable to Atrociraptor based on their long and strange serrations.
